subject: Timestamp fidelity & timezone normalization for admin-audit exports
messages:
From: compliance@heliumed.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: auditor@big4audit.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Audit export requirements — timestamps and timezone normalization

Hi Vanessa,

We're preparing for HeliumMed's SIG/SOC2 evidence collection and the external auditors asked for admin activity exports with strict timestamp fidelity. Two specific asks: 

1) All event timestamps should be provided as both ISO-8601 UTC (e.g. 2026-10-06T16:15:00Z) and the original event-local timezone (where applicable) or a timezone field.
2) Timezone normalization details and DST handling documentation for exports (how you convert and whether you store wall-clock vs normalized epoch).

Can Redwood produce a reproducible export that includes: event_id, actor, action, resource_id, raw_timestamp, normalized_timestamp_utc, timezone (IANA), and ingestion_latency_ms? Auditor wants proof we didn't normalize away forensic information.

Also include a short hash/checksum per file and a note about whether you redacted PII from the payloads. Target delivery: next Thursday (2026-10-14).

Thanks,
Maya R.
Compliance Lead — HeliumMed
compliance@heliumed.com

--
This mailbox is monitored.
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: compliance@heliumed.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit export requirements — timestamps and timezone normalization

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Quick confirmation of scope from our side: we can produce exports with both raw and normalized timestamps and include an IANA timezone field when an event contains origin timezone metadata. A few implementation notes up front:

- Source of truth: For admin console events we persist event_time as epoch-ms (UTC) at ingestion and we also capture the client-provided tz if present. For some downstream service logs we only have UTC epoch-ms (no client tz).
- Export formats: we support JSONL, CSV (RFC4180), and Parquet. Parquet will preserve types (int64 for epoch_ms, string for iso_utc).
- DST: normalized_timestamp_utc is computed from epoch-ms -> UTC. If client tz exists we include original_local_iso and local_tz (IANA). We will include a short appendix that outlines conversions and sample code.

We can provide a verifiable SHA256 checksum per archive and a signed manifest for chain-of-custody. Redaction: PII is redacted by default for exported payloads unless you request a full unredacted bundle (we'll need an approved DPA amendment).

I'll attach a draft export spec and a small sample extract for your auditors to validate. Is the auditor expecting a daily rolling export or a single point-in-time bundle for the requested window?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security Ops
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_audit_export_spec_v1.pdf, sample-admin-export-utc-parquet.gz

Thanks Vanessa — sample looks good. For the SOC2 evidence collection we prefer a sealed point-in-time bundle covering the requested assessment window (2026-07-01 through 2026-09-30). A few auditor clarifications: 

- Include ingestion_latency_ms and a short description of how you calculate it.
- Please include any upstream transforms and the exact code/version used to normalize timestamps (or at minimum the git commit id).
- A small sample of five events where the client tz was present and one where it was absent would help us confirm behavior.

We will accept Parquet or JSONL. Please add a manifest.json at the archive root that contains: file list, sha256 per file, exported_at ISO-8601 UTC, export_tool_version, and contact for verification.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Senior IT Audit — Big4Audit LLP

Team — action plan and answers to auditor asks. TL;DR: we will deliver a sealed, point-in-time bundle in Parquet plus manifest and checksums on 2026-10-14. Steps: 

1) Scope and extraction
- Marcus: generate Parquet export for window 2026-07-01 -> 2026-09-30 from admin-audit index. Fields: event_id, actor_email, action, resource_id, raw_epoch_ms, normalized_iso_utc, original_local_iso (when available), local_tz_iana, ingestion_latency_ms, raw_payload_redacted_flag.

2) Reproducibility artifacts
- Jordan: include the normalization script repo ref (git:git.prod.redwood.com/redwood/audit-export@commit: b4a7c1f) and a 2-line README describing epoch->UTC conversion and DST behavior.

3) Manifest and signing
- Kimberly: create manifest.json with file list + sha256, export_tool_version, exported_at (UTC), and sign the manifest with our internal key. Also include a cumulative sha256 of the archive (tar.gz).

4) Auditor samples and notes
- Vanessa: produce the five-event sample with mixed tz/no-tz cases and a short memo that explains cases where only UTC is available (e.g., infra logs that don't forward timezone).

5) Delivery
- We'll upload the sealed tarball to the secure evidence bucket and share a pre-signed transfer link with HeliumMed and Big4Audit by 2026-10-14 17:00 UTC. Link will be logged in HubSpot (HS-234589).

Notes/constraints: 
- Full unredacted payloads require a signed DPA amendment from HeliumMed legal (I indicated this to Maya).
- Retention: our default admin-audit retention is 13 months; if you need a longer snapshot we can request a short-term hold but will need a formal request.

I'll follow up with the pre-signed link and manifest when ready. Any objections or extra asks from the auditor?

Thanks — Vanessa
